_note: Scene catalog. views/anchors/actions are the union over `examples` and are checked against the Blender code by python/test_scene_catalog.py.

chip-teardown.description: A chip package that opens: quad flat pack, ball grid array, or a stacked AI package.

package.doc: qfp = pin-lined chip; bga = chip on balls; ai = logic die with stacked memory

seed.doc: random seed of the wire bonding

graphics-card.description: A graphics card whose cooler lifts off to show the processor underneath.

wafer.description: A silicon wafer on its chuck; one die lifts out of the grid.

cores-compare.description: Two processors side by side: a few big cores taking turns, many small ones at once.

server-racks.description: A row of server racks; one drawer slides out to show what is inside.

pull.doc: index of the rack whose drawer slides out

layer-stack.description: Named slabs dropping onto each other, bottom first; one can be the highlighted layer.

layers.doc: slab names, bottom first; anchors are layer1..layerN

neural-network.description: A feed-forward network; signals sweep through it layer by layer.

flow-diagram.description: Boxes in a row joined by traces carrying light: how one stage feeds the next.

nodes.doc: box names left to right; anchors are node1..nodeN

timeline.description: Years along a rail; each marker lights as the story reaches it.

scale-compare.description: One block beside many: how much more, counted out in cubes.

bar-chart.description: Columns rising left to right; the last one is the point of the sentence.

values.doc: column values; empty = a doubling curve

line-chart.description: A line drawn across a dark board, optionally over a row of bars.

bars.doc: optional bars under the line; adds the `bars` anchor

presenter-screen.description: A figure on a stage in front of a screen with a rising chart behind them.

people-row.description: One to six figures standing on a plinth: founders, a team, rivals.

meeting-table.description: A diner booth with people around a table and an idea sketched on a napkin.

org-radial.description: One figure at the centre, everyone else in rings around it, each linked straight in.

campus.description: A low headquarters building among trees, seen from the air.

pages.description: Front pages drifting past in the dark: attention, with nothing legible to quote.

document.description: One sheet of paper with a short title and a line that gets marked.

statement.description: A field of posts moving like a slow wave: the backdrop for a line that carries no object.

wave-slit.description: A wave meets a gap: through a wide gap it carries straight on, past a narrow one it spreads out (diffraction).

gap.doc: which gap to show; both stacks wide above narrow

grating-lens.description: Fine lines on a mask split light into a fan of beams; a lens that catches them rebuilds the lines on the wafer, a lens that misses them leaves an even glow.

mode.doc: catch: narrow fan, lines print; miss: wide fan, small lens, pattern lost; shorten: the fan narrows (shorter wavelength) until it is caught; open: the lens widens (bigger NA) until it catches the fan

formula.description: The resolution limit written out (smallest feature = k1 x wavelength / NA) with a knob under each term; the term being talked about lights up and its knob turns.

highlight.doc: which term lights up; all turns the three knobs in turn

wavelengths.description: Waves drawn to scale one above another, longest on top: how much shorter one wavelength is than another.

values.doc: wavelengths in nm, top to bottom; anchors wave1..waveN

litho-exposure.description: A projector in reverse: light through a mask, shrunk by the optics, prints the pattern into the resist on a wafer.

tin-source.description: The laser-produced-plasma source as laid out in a production scanner: tin droplets fly horizontally from a generator to a catcher; the CO2 laser comes up through the collector's central hole; a weak pulse flattens a droplet into a disc (flatten), the main pulse makes plasma and the upward-facing collector focuses its light to the intermediate focus above (ignite).

bragg-mirror.description: A cut through a multilayer mirror: every boundary reflects a weak wave, all of them leave in step, and together they make one strong reflection.

light-path.description: The route the light takes through the machine: source, collector, illuminator mirrors, the mask, six projection mirrors, the wafer; the beam fades at every bounce.

keep.doc: fraction of light each bounce keeps (sets how fast the beam fades)

scanner.description: A step-and-scan exposure: the mask and the wafer move in opposite directions, the mask four times faster, through a fixed curved slit of light with the projection optics between them; the wafer steps to the next 26 x 33 mm field and the scan runs back.

photon-rain.description: Photons land at random on a grid of resist through a slot in a mask; each square brightens with what it caught, then the print develops: with few photons the line comes out ragged.

photons.doc: about 4 or about 30 photons per square

token-stream.description: A chat window: the question at the top, the answer arriving one token at a time with an uneven rhythm (stream). With fetch, a strip below shows memory feeding a chip, one pulse per token.

prompt.doc: the question; empty = 'Why does my cat sound like a carburettor?'

answer.doc: answer tokens separated by |, a leading space marks a new word

fetch.doc: show the memory-to-chip strip (adds the `low` view and `memory`, `chip` anchors)

fiber-trip.description: A phone sends radio waves to a mast; from there the request runs as pulses of light down an optical fibre to a data centre (send); pulses come back (reply). With markers, distance ticks from 0 to 1,000 km stand along the fibre.

tokenizer.description: A sentence breaks into tokens (split), each gets its id in the vocabulary (number), each id picks out a column of numbers (embed). Defaults are a real sentence and its OpenAI o200k token ids.

tokens.doc: tokens separated by |; empty = the default sentence

ids.doc: ids separated by |, one per token

embedding-space.description: Words as points: a flat map with two coordinates lifts into a space (lift), more axes fan out for the thousands of directions (dims), an arrow and its numbers point to one word (point). Animals cluster together, far from machines.

model-layers.description: A model as a stack of layers of weights: a token's list of numbers rises through every layer, each lighting as it passes (pass); at one layer it looks back at earlier tokens, brighter links mattering more (attend).

experts.description: A mixture-of-experts layer: 128 expert blocks in a grid; for each token a router lights only four of them (route).

next-token.description: The last layer scores candidate next tokens as bars (score); one is picked and joins the sentence (pick); the model runs again and again, one token each time (loop).

next.doc: tokens appended by loop, separated by |

accelerator.description: A two-die accelerator package from above with four HBM stacks beside each die; weights stream from the stacks into the dies continuously. decode: the multipliers flash for an instant per token, then wait; prefill and batch: they stay busy (compute).

compare.description: Labelled horizontal bars with their values. race: all grow at the same speed, so a short one finishes at once while a long one keeps going; grow: they rise together. A value lo-hi draws a range.

wire-trip.description: A number fetched from a distant memory chip crawls down a long wire that warms as it passes to a multiplier (send); a number from the register next door arrives at once (local).

hbm-stack.description: A high-bandwidth-memory stack beside a two-die GPU on a silicon interposer: a base logic die with DRAM dies on top joined by microbumps and through-silicon vias; it comes apart (explode) and the vias and interposer wires light (signal).

batching.description: One fetch of the weights feeds many conversations at once, each getting its next token (share). single: one conversation only. cache: each conversation also keeps a growing column of notes and the memory fills toward its limit (adds the `cache` view).

bit-width.description: A weight written with sixteen bits shrinks to four (shrink); two lanes of the same width carry numbers to a chip, four times as many at four bits (flow).

gpu-rack.description: A rack laid out like a GB200 NVL72: power shelves, ten and eight compute trays of four GPUs around nine switch trays, a copper cable spine at the back, liquid manifolds. pull: one tray slides out to show two GPUs and a CPU per board under cold plates; link: the spine lights; slice: the 72 GPUs light in groups; cool: coolant runs.

heat-loop.description: A rack hands its heat to a coolant loop, a coolant distribution unit passes it to facility water, which runs to a mechanical-draft cooling tower where a little water evaporates and the vapour carries the heat away (flow, evaporate).

chip-factory.description: Inside a chip drawn as a factory floor: twelve desks of multipliers with workers (pixel-art sprites and glossy toy figures mixed), a memory tower far to the left, a road and a gate between them, a little truck carrying a glowing load of weights. Default: most workers doze, waiting; busy: every desk lit and every worker awake (prefill or a big batch). deliver: the truck drives from memory to the gate and the desks flash once.

truck_x.doc: where the truck stands on the road before any delivery

seed.doc: which desks get which kind of worker

poses.doc: per-desk poses separated by | (sleep, wait, sit, work); empty = mostly asleep

guides.doc: stand the explorer and the token by the road (cast does this per shot instead)

word.doc: the token the guide token carries

vienna.description: Vienna in the 1840s: plastered houses on cobbled streets, chimney smoke, lamps a lamplighter lights one by one, windows lighting house by house, people walking and greeting; the general hospital across the end of the main street with one open lit window where Semmelweis writes at his desk. The streets are dressed: shop awnings and signboards, shutters and balconies, a market with sellers and buyers, handcarts pushed along, barrels and crates by the doors, a pump, trees by the hospital, washing across the back streets, birds over the roofs, neighbours talking. The court has cobbles, a pump, benches, trees, a stretcher carried across, students talking; the assistant's room has books, papers, a candle and a bed; the dissecting room has jars on shelves, a basin and late students.

time.doc: time of day; a>b changes over the beat

lit.doc: share of window storeys that light

lights_from.doc: windows start lighting at this fraction of the beat

lights_until.doc: all lit windows are on by this fraction

lamps_from.doc: the lamplighter starts at this fraction

lamps_until.doc: the last lamp is lit at this fraction

walkers.doc: people on the main street (the first two meet and greet)

tint.doc: brightness of the street people (dim at night)

groups.doc: groups of two or three neighbours standing and talking by the house fronts

birds.doc: a flock crossing over the roofs

asylum.description: 1865, night: a high wall with an arched gate under a flickering lantern; guards bring a man in, their shadows on the wall; a cell with a barred window, moonlight, a door that shuts. Violence is implied, never shown. The cell has a barred window with moonlight falling through it onto straw, a bucket, a stool and a chain.

drag_from.doc: the guards start walking him in (fraction)

ward.description: Vienna General Hospital, the First Obstetric Clinic, 1846: a long whitewashed ward (24 x 8 x 5 m) with a beamed ceiling, tall windows on one side letting in cool daylight, a worn plank floor. Two rows of seven iron beds with straw mattresses, a woman lying in most of them (pixel billboards, their faces worried or sad; a few beds stripped with folded linen), tin cups and jugs on small night tables, a crucifix on the far wall, a wash stand with basin and towel and a linen cupboard (water only: no chlorine yet), and by the door a table with the register and an oil lamp. A doctor and three students examine at the first bed, a midwife goes from bed to bed and stops to talk, a woman in labour is held up by a second midwife. Action bell: the priest carrying the viaticum and the altar boy ringing a bell come in at the far door and walk the aisle to a bed; the patients they pass turn their heads and look worried. Daylight by day; at dusk and night a few oil lamps are lit.

time.doc: time of day; a>b changes over the beat (more oil lamps are lit at dusk and night)

seed.doc: which patients look which way, how the group talks
